blocks.text: **Inclusive growth** is growth that is **broad-based across sectors and regions, employment-intensive, and poverty-reducing**, with **equality of opportunity** in access to markets, resources and services (the World Bank/OECD framing India's 11th Plan — 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth' — adopted). It has **process and outcome** dimensions: participation (who produces the growth) and benefit-sharing (who consumes it). Measures: poverty headcounts (**MPI** — health/education/living standards; Tendulkar-line legacy), **inequality** (Gini ~0.35–0.40 consumption; wealth far higher), **employment** (LFPR, worker-population ratio, informality ~90%), and access gaps (financial, digital, health, learning).

rows: **Economic**
Landless labour, informal workers, micro-enterprises
No assets or credit; casualised work without social security; the 'missing middle' denies formal jobs
**Social**
SCs, STs, minorities, women, persons with disabilities
Historical discrimination; caste-occupation lock-in; unpaid care burden; the tribal land-alienation frontier
**Regional/spatial**
Eastern & central India; within states — e.g., **Rayalaseema & north-coastal AP vs the Krishna-Godavari delta**
Geography + infrastructure deficits + colonial investment patterns; agro-climatic disadvantage
**Financial & digital**
The unbanked/under-banked; smartphone-less households
Documentation, distance, digital literacy — exclusion by authentication in the DBT era
**Knowledge/health**
First-generation learners, undernourished children
Learning poverty (ASER gaps), stunting ~35% (NFHS-5), anaemia — capability exclusion before market entry

sections.heading: Causes of exclusion in India — the deep drivers

items: **Initial conditions**: colonial deindustrialisation + zamindari legacies concentrated assets; land reform succeeded only patchily (WB, Kerala, and — for tenancy recording — undivided Andhra's protected-tenant laws partially).
**Growth pattern**: services-led, skill-biased growth rewards the educated urban minority; agriculture's terms of trade and productivity stagnation hold back the largest workforce.

**Social structure**: caste and gender as allocation mechanisms — occupational inheritance, discrimination in labour/credit markets (audit-study evidence), child-marriage/care norms cutting female LFPR.
**State capacity gaps**: schooling without learning, PHCs without doctors, titles without records — services reach unevenly, so public provision fails as the equaliser.

**Informality trap**: 90% informal employment → no pensions/insurance → shocks (illness, COVID) liquidate assets → poverty re-entry; migration's inclusion (remittances) and exclusion (portability of rights — the e-Shram/ONORC answer).
**Political economy**: elite capture of subsidies, regional bargaining power differences, and the fiscal squeeze on the social sector (health ~2%, education ~3% of GDP vs 2.5/6 goals).

sections.heading: The AP lens and answer craft

items: **AP's inclusion profile**: strong on delivery-inclusion (near-universal PDS, DBT saturation, Aarogyasri, high financial-inclusion metrics via SHG-bank linkage) — weaker on **structural inclusion** (farm-wage dependence, regional gaps: Rayalaseema's drought belt and the tribal agency's deprivation vs delta prosperity; female work concentrated in low-wage agriculture/aqua processing).

**Craft**: define (process + outcome) → five-dimension exclusion table → six deep causes → one paragraph of evidence (MPI exit of 13.5 crore nationally; NFHS-5 stunting/anaemia; informality 90%) → AP's two-speed profile. The 'circle of exclusion' diagram organises everything.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Distinguish inclusion from mere redistribution — the examiner wants opportunity-equality language (assets, capabilities, access) with the causal circle, not a scheme list. Save schemes for the next note; here, analysis wins.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — measuring inclusion & the drivers of exclusion

items: **Measures to cite:** **Gini coefficient** (income inequality), **Palma ratio** (top-10%/bottom-40%), **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, **HDI/IHDI**, and financial-inclusion indices (RBI FI-Index).

**Rangarajan vs Tendulkar poverty lines** — the methodological debate; NITI Aayog's national MPI shows a sharp fall in the multidimensionally poor (large numbers escaping poverty), even as **income inequality** (World Inequality Lab data on top-1%/10% shares) remains high.
**Deep drivers of exclusion:** caste and gender, regional imbalance, informality (~90% of workers), asset/land inequality, digital divide, and inadequate human capital.

**AP lens:** DBT-saturation, SHG-led inclusion and near-universal welfare access are the state's inclusion levers; the test is whether they raise **capabilities (Sen)** and productive employment, not just transfers.

prelimsPointers: **Gini coefficient** ranges 0 (perfect equality) to 1; **Palma ratio** = top 10% ÷ bottom 40% income share.
**Tendulkar (2009) and Rangarajan (2014)** committees revised India's poverty-line methodology.
11th Five-Year Plan (2007–12): **'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'** — the phrase's official Indian debut.
**MPI (NITI/UNDP)**: ~**13.5 crore exited multidimensional poverty** 2015-16 → 2019-21; dimensions — health, education, living standards.
**NFHS-5 (2019-21)**: stunting ~35.5%, women's anaemia ~57% — capability-exclusion markers.
Informal employment ≈ **90%** of India's workforce (PLFS-based estimates).
**ONORC (One Nation One Ration Card)** enables PDS portability for migrants — inclusion-by-portability.
**e-Shram**: national database of unorganised workers (30+ crore registered).
Consumption **Gini ~0.35–0.40**; wealth inequality far higher (top 1% ~40% of wealth by some estimates).
mainsAngles: Define inclusive growth in its process and outcome senses and explain why GDP growth alone missed the excluded.
Map the dimensions of exclusion in India and trace their mutually reinforcing circle.
Caste, gender and geography still allocate opportunity in India — examine with evidence.
Informality is the institutional form of exclusion — discuss with the social-security and portability responses.
Andhra Pradesh delivers welfare inclusively but grows unevenly — analyse the state's two-speed inclusion profile.

glossary.definition: Growth that is broad-based, employment-generating and poverty-reducing, with equal opportunity of access — participation plus benefit-sharing.
Denial of access to markets, assets, credit and decent work that keeps groups outside the growth process.
Inability to read an age-appropriate text by age 10 — schooling-without-learning as capability exclusion.
Appropriation of public benefits by locally powerful groups, diverting inclusion instruments from intended beneficiaries.
Making rights (rations, health cover) claimable anywhere in India — the migrant-inclusion reform exemplified by ONORC.
Strong transfer-based welfare coexisting with weak structural transformation — high delivery, lagging opportunity.

sections.heading: The instrument stack — poverty and employment

rows: **MGNREGA (2005)**
Legal right: 100 days/rural household; demand-driven; wage floor; assets + social audit
Self-targeting works; drought insurance function proven (COVID surge to ~11 crore individuals); critiques — budget as rationing device, wage delays, asset quality
**NRLM/Aajeevika**
SHG federations + bank linkage + livelihoods (the **AP SERP model nationalised**)
~10 crore women mobilised; credit access transformed; graduation to enterprises still thin
₹6,000/yr unconditional to landholder farmers
Fast, leak-proof DBT; excludes tenants & labourers — the AP counterpoint: Rythu Bharosa topped up and (in design) included tenants via crop-cultivator rights
**PMAY-G/U**
Housing with DBT + geo-tagging
~3+ crore rural houses; asset-based poverty exit; land for the landless remains the binding constraint
**Social security floor**

PM-JJBY/PMSBY (insurance ~₹2 lakh at ₹20-436/yr), APY (pension), e-Shram; NSAP old-age pensions (₹200-500 central — states top up: **AP's pensions among India's most generous ~₹4,000/month via doorstep delivery**)
Coverage widening; adequacy (central NSAP amounts frozen) the weak point

sections.heading: Health and education — the capability instruments

items: **Health**: **Ayushman Bharat's two legs** — PM-JAY (₹5 lakh hospitalisation cover; ~55 crore target; AP's own **Aarogyasri (2007)** pioneered the model and runs an expanded state version — NTR Vaidya Seva lineage, cover raised toward ₹25 lakh) + **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** (1.6+ lakh upgraded primary centres); National Health Mission (ASHA army); challenges — OOPE still ~40-45%, workforce gaps, primary-tertiary imbalance; **AP's family-doctor programme (2023)** — village-level physician visits pairing with secretariats: a cite-worthy state innovation.

**Education**: RTE 2009 (near-universal enrolment) → the learning crisis (ASER: ~half of class-V can't read class-II text) → **NEP 2020's** response (FLN mission — NIPUN Bharat; 5+3+3+4; mother-tongue foundation); PM POSHAN (mid-day meals; **AP's Gorumudda** with eggs/chikki enrichment), scholarships & fee reimbursement (**AP's full fee reimbursement for eligible students** — the state's signature education-inclusion instrument alongside school-infrastructure upgrades and English-medium transition, with its bilingual-pedagogy debate).

**The design lesson across all instruments**: rights + DBT + saturation beat discretionary targeting; but **transfers buy floors, not ladders** — capability instruments (learning, health, skills) convert floors into mobility: the two-generation strategy.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The floor-vs-ladder distinction is the analytical spine: transfers stop deprivation today; health-education-skills end its inheritance. Close every instruments answer with the two-generation strategy line.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the poverty, employment & capability instruments

items: **Employment:** **MGNREGA** (rural wage-employment guarantee, 100 days), **DAY-NRLM/NULM**, **PM-SVANidhi** (street vendors), **skilling (PMKVY, Skill India)**, and the gig-worker social-security push under the Code on Social Security.
**Poverty/income support:** **DBT**, **PM-KISAN** (₹6,000/yr to farmers), **PMGKAY** (free foodgrains to ~80 crore under NFSA), and pensions (NSAP).

**Capability instruments — health:** **Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY, ₹5 lakh cover), Health & Wellness Centres/Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**; **education:** **RTE, NEP 2020, Samagra Shiksha, PM POSHAN (mid-day meal), PM SHRI schools**.
**Sen's capability approach:** development = expanding real freedoms/capabilities, not just income — the theoretical spine for any inclusive-growth answer.

**PM-KISAN** — ₹6,000 per year to eligible farmers in three instalments.

**NSAP** central pensions remain ₹200–500/month; AP tops up to ~**₹4,000/month with doorstep delivery** — among India's highest.

Covering all eligible rather than phased targeting — minimising exclusion errors; AP welfare's operating principle.
Reading with comprehension and basic arithmetic by grade 3 — the gateway capability NEP 2020 prioritises.

sections.heading: Women's empowerment — the economics of half the sky

blocks.text: Women's empowerment is **agency + assets + income + voice** — not scheme receipt alone. The macro case: raising female LFPR (**~35-37% and rising on recent PLFS from a ~23% low — much of it rural self-employment; quality is the question**) toward parity could add double-digit GDP percentages (IMF/McKinsey). The instrument stack works four channels: **economic** (SHG-credit, PMMY Mudra — ~68% women borrowers, Stand-Up India, DAY-NULM), **security & rights** (PWDVA, POSH, Shakti Sadans/One-Stop Centres, reservation), **capability** (Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, scholarships, Sukanya Samriddhi), and **time/infrastructure** (Ujjwala ~10 crore LPG connections, Jal Jeevan tap water, maternity benefits — PMMVY, crèches) — the last freeing the unpaid-care hours that block work.

rows: Livelihood & credit
NRLM (10 crore SHG women), Mudra, Stand-Up India, Lakhpati Didi (crorewomen-scale goal)
**SERP/Velugu federations** — the national NRLM template; **Cheyutha/Aasara-type asset & bank-linkage transfers**; aqua & dairy value-chain groups
Protection
POSH 2013, PWDVA 2005, Mission Shakti (OSCs, helplines), fast-track courts
**Disha police stations & the proposed Disha law** (fast-track for offences against women); Mahila police volunteers
Capability & health
BBBP, Sukanya Samriddhi, PMMVY (₹5,000+), Poshan Abhiyaan
Girl-child education incentives, menstrual-health programmes in schools, anaemia mission (NFHS-5 AP women's anaemia high — the target)
Voice & representation
**106th Amendment** (1/3 in LS/Assemblies, post-delimitation); PRI reservation
**50% reservation in AP local bodies**; SHG federations as parallel women's parliaments

sections.heading: Social welfare schemes — the wider net, and the tests

items: **Life-cycle logic**: ICDS/Poshan (0–6) → PM POSHAN & scholarships (school) → skills/Mudra (youth) → maternity & health cover (working age) → NSAP/state pensions (old age) — evaluate any welfare portfolio by its life-cycle coverage and gaps (adolescent girls and the elderly-care economy are the thin patches).

**Vulnerable-group schemes**: SC/ST — post-matric scholarships (DBT-reformed), Stand-Up India, **SCSP/TSP fund earmarking (an S.R. Sankaran-era legacy)**; PwD — Accessible India, ADIP; elderly — IGNOAPS plus state top-ups; transgender persons — SMILE; minorities — PM-VIKAS.

**The four tests for evaluating any welfare scheme** (use in every answer): **adequacy** (is the amount meaningful?), **coverage** (exclusion errors?), **delivery** (leakage? dignity?), **graduation** (does it build exit routes?). AP scores high on coverage-delivery, contested on adequacy-vs-fiscal-space and graduation.

**The empowerment caveat**: transfers to women's accounts improve household bargaining (evidence) but **agency needs assets in her name** (land titles, house pattas — AP's practice of registering housing pattas in women's names is the cite), mobility, and freedom from violence — measure empowerment by decisions, not disbursements.

blocks.text: Exam tip: The examiner's discriminator is the empowerment-vs-welfare distinction. Two sentences do it: welfare gives her benefits; empowerment gives her the pen — the account, the patta, the seat, the safe street. Then prove AP's SHG lineage makes it the natural laboratory.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — women's empowerment economics & the welfare test

items: **The economic case:** closing the gender gap in labour-force participation could raise GDP substantially (IMF/McKinsey); India's **female LFPR** has risen (PLFS) but remains low and heavily rural/agricultural; unpaid care work is the hidden constraint.

**Instruments:** SHGs (DAY-NRLM), **Lakhpati Didi**, **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, maternity benefit (26 weeks), **106th Amendment (women's reservation)**, and financial inclusion (Jan Dhan accounts majority women).

**The welfare-scheme test (any scheme):** **targeting** (exclusion/inclusion errors), **leakage** (DBT fixes), **fiscal cost**, **incentive effects**, and **outcome vs outlay** — apply this grid to critique or defend any programme.
**AP dimension:** among the highest SHG mobilisation of women; women-centric DBT (e.g., support to mothers for children's education/health) — a national reference for gender-focused delivery.

mainsAngles: 'Women's empowerment is smart economics, not just social justice' — substantiate with data and Andhra Pradesh's SHG experience.

prelimsPointers: Female LFPR rose to ~**35-37%** (PLFS recent rounds) from ~23% (2017-18) — largely rural self-employment.
**PM Mudra Yojana**: ~68% of loan accounts are women's; Stand-Up India mandates one woman borrower per bank branch.
**Ujjwala**: ~10 crore LPG connections; time-poverty and indoor-air-pollution instrument.
**PMMVY**: ₹5,000 maternity benefit (first child; ₹6,000 for second girl child) — Art 42's statutory echo via NFSA Sec 4.
**106th Amendment (2023)**: women's reservation in LS/Assemblies after delimitation; **AP local bodies already reserve 50%**.
**SCSP/TSP**: plan-fund earmarking proportionate to SC/ST population — institutionalised in undivided AP by statute (2013 Act).
AP registers **house pattas in women's names** — asset-based empowerment practice.
**Lakhpati Didi**: NRLM goal of SHG women earning ₹1 lakh+ annually (3 crore target).
mainsAngles: Welfare gives benefits, empowerment gives agency — distinguish and evaluate India's women-centric instrument stack.
Female labour-force participation is rising but its quality is contested — analyse with PLFS evidence and the care-economy constraint.
The SHG movement is India's largest women's institution — trace its AP origins and assess its empowerment record.
Evaluate India's social welfare architecture on the life-cycle principle, identifying the thin patches.
Assets in her name change the household's arithmetic — discuss with land titles, housing pattas and bank accounts.

glossary.definition: The capacity to make and act on one's own choices — the empowerment criterion beyond income or benefit receipt.
Deficit of discretionary time from unpaid care and drudgery — the invisible tax on women's work and leisure.
Designing social protection to cover risks at each life stage from infancy to old age — the completeness test of welfare systems.
A member's influence over household decisions, shifted by her income, assets, exit options and legal protections.
Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan and Tribal Sub-Plan — earmarking development funds proportionate to SC/ST population shares.
Sakhi centres providing integrated police, legal, medical and shelter support to women facing violence.
